title: Delinquency Notice, Default and Cure — Apartment Home Lease Collections Standard
content:
This collections standard governs the statutory notice demanding past-due rent (pay rent or quit) on an Apartment Home Lease, the default it opens and how that default is cured.

## 1. Serving a notice

1.1 A delinquency notice may be served only on an active lease, as the lease record shows.

1.2 A delinquency notice may be served only when the frozen date is later than the rent due date of the billing period plus the effective grace period. Grace days are counted as calendar days starting the day after the rent due date, without skipping weekends or holidays, so the first late day is the day after the last grace day. The due date is read from the period's rent line on the ledger and the community's state from the lease record.

1.3 The effective grace period is the one defined by the late fee rule.

1.4 No notice is served for a billing period covered by a signed payment plan in good standing.

1.5 Service is by personal delivery or by posting and mailing.

## 2. What the notice demands

2.1 The amount demanded is the unpaid rent only — the sum of the unpaid rent of every late billing period on the notice date — and never includes late fees, returned payment fees, other lease fees or charges of any other charter. The notice records the latest rent month included.

2.2 The unpaid rent of a period is its base rent and prorated rent, less the rent concession and program discount credits of that period, less the part of the payments received by that day (net of returns) that is assigned to that period's rent, never below zero.

## 3. Notice period and cure deadline

3.1 The notice period is the number of days fixed for the community's state. The day of service is not counted. In California the period counts only days that are not Saturdays, Sundays or California court holidays; in every other state it counts calendar days, the last one included even when it falls on a weekend. The cure deadline is the last day of that period.

| State of the community | Notice period (days) | Days counted |
|---|---|---|
| California (CA) | 3 | days that are not Saturdays, Sundays or California court holidays |
| Washington (WA) | 14 | calendar days |
| Colorado (CO) | 10 | calendar days |
| Texas (TX) | 3 | calendar days |
| Georgia (GA) | 3 | calendar days |
| Arizona (AZ) | 5 | calendar days |

## 4. Default and cure

4.1 Serving the notice puts the lease in default.

4.2 The default is cured, and the lease returns to active, when before the file is referred to eviction counsel the payments received on or after the notice date reach the amount demanded, or the resident signs a payment plan and pays its down payment. Rent that fell due after the notice date is not part of the cure amount.

4.3 A payment received after a referral never cures the default.

## 5. Worked dates (hypothetical)

- **Earliest service.** Rent due 1 May with an effective grace period of 3 days: the grace days are 2, 3 and 4 May, and the first late day is 5 May. A notice may be served on 5 May; on 4 May it may not, because 4 May is not later than the due date plus the grace period.
- **Washington.** Served Monday 3 March 2025: the 14 days run 4 through 17 March, so the cure deadline is 17 March 2025.
- **Texas.** Served Friday 7 March 2025: the 3 days are 8, 9 and 10 March, the weekend counted, so the cure deadline is Monday 10 March 2025.
- **California.** Served Thursday 6 March 2025, with no court holiday in the window: the counted days are Friday 7, Monday 10 and Tuesday 11 March, so the cure deadline is 11 March 2025.
- **Cure amount.** A notice demanding $1,900.00 served on 20 April: payments received from 20 April totalling $1,900.00 before any referral cure the default, even though the May rent that fell due after the notice date remains open.
